heading: Backtracking with unlimited reuse
body: Use the **same index** when you recurse to allow picking the same candidate again. A **start index** prevents duplicate permutations ([2,3] vs [3,2]). Sort first to prune early when a candidate exceeds the target.

heading: How to recognize it
body: Look for **"find all combinations"** + **"unlimited reuse"** (same element many times). Classic backtracking pattern: choose → recurse → unchoose (pop).

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we pass the same index `i` (not `i+1`) to the recursive call?
options: To allow unlimited reuse of the same candidate
explain: Passing `i` (not `i+1`) allows the recursion to pick the same candidate multiple times.
